en: Love as bowl, devotion as oil
the mind melting with bliss as a wick to be put, well melting
I lifted the glowing lamp of cognition
I who made expert Tamil for Nāraṇaṉ
If one perceives well by cognition the names of Nāraṇaṉ
[and] moreover pronounces his names in [his] place, [that] will make
[us] into immortals adorning heaven. That is, isn’t it
the nature of our king of the humble immortals
Those who worship the feet of the one from the milk ocean
with excellent fragrant blossoms, it seems as if they will get to enter
the city of the king of good immortals, with an appearance of light
that shines with the aural teaching of the ancient immortals who worship [him]
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
participial noun, imperfective aspect, plural, third person
participial noun, imperfective aspect, plural, honorific, third person

en: Building a temple, taking day[-fresh] blossoms with [dew] pearls, there
combining [them] with glittering sapphires [and] diamonds
offering incomparable fresh lotus I humbled myself before the feet of him
who took her from the dewy [lotus] blossom onto the right of [his] body
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect

en: You who, it seems, that day in three steps measured the world
you who took the earth by begging for three steps, tall Māl
with a body [the colour of] the flood waters who stood on earth
who can know [and] sing about your feet?
gloss: participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect

en: As those whose minds are filled with affection, knowingly controlling
all five [senses] within [and] taking choice flowers, the great ascetics
who praise reciting the names of him who has understood right, will see [them]
the ankleted [feet] of him with the colour of the rain flood
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect

en: [The foot with] an anklet rising, mouth twisting, eyes rolling
so that the enemies, their spirits caught in fire, were scared
he lifted the fire-raising battle discus. Regard his red feet
golden [lotus] blossoms; immerse yourself, o heart, joyfully
She who joyfully inclined [her] light-coloured breast to you
[and] said ‘drink so as to cool [your] insides’, [acting] as if you joyfully
drank from [her] breast you drank [her] soul in hatred
grace to your flexible nature, that day
gloss: participial noun, singular, feminine, perfective aspect

en: The cowherdess, who that day was without fear seeing that
took pity on you [and] constantly gave you [her] breast, will she
in return for this disposition, justly reach the world surrounded by the great sea
that you measured in superior fashion that day?
Me who has a [skilful] tongue
that praised as the guardian of many lives, him who as a child
destroyed the horse cart, who begged for [and] protected the earth
me with flowers, for thinking of you constantly
protect [me] who am [your] servant, at the end that comes
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, accusative, perfective aspect
participial noun, masculine singular, accusative, perfective aspect

en: Standing in the entry, worshipping the ankleted [feet] of the immortals daily
they will be people with mediocre pleasures. Tall Māl
with the water-flood body who stands at the side
who are those capable of reciting [verses] about your feet?
He is not that one [or] this one. Who will not bow
[and] praise the feet of him on the serpent bed? Many without count
besides him with ample rays, him on the bright blossom [and] him with the forehead eye
are bound to worship [him] day after day
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
participial noun, honorific, third person, negative

en: The huge elephant that established a link, fearfully entering into the enclosed tank
with fresh lotus taken up thoughfully, when he was piled with affliction
that day, didn’t he humble himself before the feet of him with the discus?
He once reached the abode of the king of celestials
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: Without talking to those who live here with guilt [and] sin
making [their] bellies great places, o foolish people, reciting the names
of the one possessing four arms that stretch to all eight directions
turn [to him and] make yourselves pure
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, honorific, third person

en: That he wandered, urging the chariot in hot battle, that day
that he separated from Sītā, going after the deer, and that he
to have a bed on the ground is that [so] beautiful[ly done] by the one
who has [his] cool bed on the snake?
gloss: neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun
verbal noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect
neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun
participial noun, masculine singular, imperfective aspect

en: Falling in servitude to him, even if one does not know it
is holding Māl so that he is close to [one’s] mind. Except for this
when one acts in a manner that a sand bank in the forest may become a lake
who else will be able to pour the rain?
gloss: neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun
concessive, conditional, negative, singular, first person
neuter singular, imperfective aspect, verbal noun

en: Are there others to rival [him]? Going after the worker to whom all around
the king of the celestials [and] the one on the great flower bow
the one with red matted hair in which the unique crescent moon sits took
his request to Māl, begged [and] succeeded
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: That he took the world in the form of a dwarf, that, in the form of a murderous
lion, he put [his] nails in the chest of the bright forceful man, and that he ate
the seven worlds crossed by him [is good] conduct practiced by Māl with lotus eyes
the one who crossed the sky in one day
gloss: verbal noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect
verbal noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect
neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun
participial noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: It is not [good] conduct; look, you who destroyed the strong cart
you need not think it is [good] conduct, evil Tirumāl
who threw the young calf after the fruits of the evil wood-apple tree
you committed a crime, so that it is evident to the world
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, singular, second person

en: Warding off sin [and] evil with [their] hands, those who live [with] you
as the path for a long time, won’t they live?
It is them who possess the means to perceive well without fault
the names of Nāraṇaṉ [and] to praise [him] well
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, honorific, third person

en: They exist, their minds are inside, there are lotus
flowers, there is time for praising. For those whose heads
connect with the blessed feet of the dwarf
it is rare that they go straight to harsh hell
What is difficult becomes easy, if one finds those who make
an effort to change [and] improve by [their own] strength
The unique huge elephant that is black with white tusks accomplished victory
bowing low with a big blossom on a cool twig
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, accusative, honorific, third person

en: He will let live those who pass [their] time bowing low
taking boons, living in befitting ways
he who threw the calf onto the hanging wood-apple fruits [and], in another form
measured the world [and] took it under [his] foot
gloss: participial noun, accusative, imperfective aspect, honorific, third person

en: Look at him, good heart: rare grace and loss
he [is]. Look, he stands as the five senses. Look
wind, fire, water, sky, black mountain, earth, the rain flood
the fire of anger he becomes, too, in turn
gloss: imperfective aspect, singular, masculine, third person

en: He came [and] went straight to Laṅkā, killed Rāvaṇa
with his anger, when one talks about it, and he stands
on Vēṅkaṭam with cool slopes high with bamboo, the one
of high ancient praise in the mouth of the celestials
gloss: verbal noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect
neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun
participial noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect

en: Praising, restraining inside all five of the five senses
that were on the way to him, driving [them] affectionately
the immortals of the earth will live in the abode given
of old to the immortals, because of [their] deeds as immortals by rank
The mind that settles in a place [but] rises, searching, growing
resembles a shoot that looks up to the sky, rubbing against the moon
with increasing speed, running in search of a good support
the mind that runs in search of Māl
gloss: participial noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect

en: Those who say ‘Lord’, daily always at great dawn
those who, with the good rich buds of the Kurā[-tree] throw themselves
at the feet of the one with the decorative form of a boar look!
will joyfully see [his] sapphire form
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: Exulted is [my] mind, o Tirumāl, moreover
exulted, praising your feet, exulted
singing of these: the fiery diskus [and] the conch
with concentration, encompassing [your] body in the act of dancing
gloss: participial noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect
participial noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect

en: Concentrated is [my] mind, inwardly, on the names of him who decorates
[his] body with tulsi garlands, and it humbled itself many times
before the one from victorious Vēṅkatam, with bamboo-glittering slopes
in the [same] way that [my] mouth speaks of [his] qualities
gloss: participial noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect
participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect
participial noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect

en: Praising the feet of you, who once had begged for and by that way
measured the earth, [and] with incense [and] fragrant blossoms
practicing love that is very exulted, I have fallen in servitude to you now
by my good fortune
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, singular, second person

en: Sweet, they say, is passion, and sweeter than that
they say, is cool river water, o my father. If they
without desiring passion [and] water as sweet, desire your greatness
[your] protection has become [their] nature, a little bit
gloss: conditional, imperfective aspect, honorific, third person

en: All the ignorant ones
who attain in what is little the greatness of little ones
they are ignorant ones. Without knowing think:
‘the Dark one who has taken, eaten [and] spit out the world,’
my heart, [and] stick [to it]
You who gave [the world] him with perfect faces in [all the four] directions
in the brilliant blossom of the big cool lotus, if we do not
befittingly praise your feet [and] humble ourselves, for many births
we [shall] have all afflictions
gloss: participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect

en: When is the great treasure not bewildering to us?
For them, always knowing support, for us
creating a mind that always says ‘Mātavaṉ’, moreover
reciting his names with the tongue is the Recitation
gloss: neuter singular, imperfective aspect, verbal noun

en: To the extent that it fullfills the meaning of the recitation know, foolish people
the way to praise the names of the Highest. If you don’t master that as a recitation
if you don’t discern it well, [then] speaking the name of Mātavaṉ
is an abridgement of the recitation
gloss: pronominalised noun, conditional, plural, second person
neuter singular, imperfective aspect, verbal noun

en: As a shortcut, dragging, moving around, standing, without first
nearing doubt-filled people, you think, see:
there is no sense in enjoyment that does not know
although it knows, the feet of him on whose chest Śrī is flourishing
By wealth, there is no entering and progressing into the immortal world
By grace, isn’t Dharma also grace? The sapphire-coloured one
who by grace alone gave [himself] to the great Veda expert, his feet
don’t you forget, heart, think [of them]
gloss: pronominalised noun, dative, honorific, third person

en: I think of Tirumāl in order to see his extended arms
Those who think [thus] are not due for [another] birth. Those born
in the house, those who worship those arms have abandoned
all the great pleasures obtained from being born
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, honorific, third person
participial noun, honorific, third person, negative
participial noun, perfective aspect, honorific, third person
participial noun, negative, honorific, third person

en: Who will worship the two feet of him who shot the arrow so that the two
[times] eight arms, all the seven [and] three heads and both feet fell?
Worshipping those feet, isn’t it, is the honour
my excellent arms do [to them]
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect
neuter singular, imperfective aspect, verbal noun

en: The names of red-eyed Māl are the high[est] aid to the best people
I don’t hold with those who, being human, have forgotten [them]
Having created a mind that says, ‘o Mātavaṉ who upholds the Dharma’
remember moreover to recite his names with the tongue
gloss: participial noun, dative, perfective aspect, honorific, third person
participial noun, accusative, perfective aspect, honorific, third person
participial noun, negative, singular, first person
neuter singular, imperfective aspect, verbal noun

en: Those who are exulted, saying ‘it is’, don’t go anywhere near
what is weak, saying ‘it is not’ residing at the feet of him who has feet
touched by the heads of the celestials, the one from Vēṅkaṭam
the one of the Veda who is difficult to measure
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, honorific, third person

en: He is resident in [Tiruv]araṅkam [and] Tirukkōṭṭi and since many days
is he resident in Vēṅkaṭam, since many days he is resident
in ornate glittering Cōlai [and] on the decorative Nīrmalai
Māl with liberal broad hands who glitters [like] a sapphire
gloss: neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun
neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun
neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun

en: Adorning the foot-blossoms of him in lion-form with a garland
rise in worship in the morning joining [your] hands [and]
perceiving no other but the majesty who measured, dug out, ate
[and] spit out the earth, in the way that [he] lies inside [you]
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: You realised all four Vedas, you recited the rules [of conduct]
you joined the shoulders of the girl on the flower, o Māl, you went [and] joined
the mountain Māliruñcōlai surrounded by the wide dark earth
with slopes dark with bamboo
The seven mountains and the seven great continents and the seven noisy seas
that thunderingly surround the banks, invoke, my heart
without being afraid, as the One with a tongue that, prattling to the woman
drank [her life] force along with the poison contained in [her] breast
I invoke Tirumāl, saying the great names
without fault, [as] spoken by those there envisioning him
who is addressed ‘o cowherd difficult to scrutinize, o Yātavaṉ,’
as Māyavaṉ before all people
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, accusative, perfective aspect

en: Envision mentally, heart, the feet of him with sapphire colour
envision mentally, again, his names, envision mentally
the colour of him of water-ocean hue, who, coming from
the great ocean, churned the [milk] sea
Who is black in colour, who has on [his] chest her of the big red [lotus] blossom
who is great in Dharma who are those that know it
the path of him who sent the one resembling a Rākṣasa with a sword, who committed braveries
for a long stay at the site of the king of celestials?
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, accusative, imperfective aspect
participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect

en: Vēṅkaṭam is the mountain we long for, called a hill
with dashing floods where flower creepers stay without letting loose
unwittingly thinking the masses of curls, that stay in front [and] hang down
the backs of those of the [religious] path, are a young mountain
gloss: participial noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect

en: Thinking ‘don’t abandon the temporary temple in the flood’
I remember, having kept it in [my] heart as [my] inner temple
as a station equal in essense [to those] that you esteem as stations
[namely] both these: Iruñcōlai [and] Vēṅkaṭam that are mountains
I never forget, because of [my] nature
that never stops thinking constantly of the seven births
O knowing one with the victorious, murderous discus
You of the ocean of bliss, look [at me] graciously
If one exceedingly shows much love in order to see [him]
if one says ‘she is shy’, will she [then] be shy before
she reverentially shows black Māl as a golden body
Śrī who shows us Tirumāl?
Look, fullfill the task of lauding with [your] tongues the god
who is ever gracious towards the young woman Śrī. Suitably
we praised the names of our Father, with large feet [and] broad hands
did you hear it in all four directions?
All the goodness we obtain is by the grace of the tongue Lady
who gives the essence of grace by keeping [us] protected in [her] good heart
making us recite, saying ‘even if the essence of [earthly] riches
is like a Neem fruit, sing of the golden discus.’
Directing my mind which longs for grace on [his] servants
understanding the meaning at that time [I] had the sight, roaming in the darkness
I looked; looking, I thought and considering, ‘that is the bright lotus’
I thus raised myself
You do not have a single form; the light form is your form
‘He has two forms,’ they say, they of the vast land, who have understood
the manner in which in the beginning there was one form. They, see
constantly guard the earth according to the rule
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
participial noun, honorific, third person, perfective aspect

en: One foot stood, the arms lengthened so as to cover the ground
in going it measured all the directions, they say, o robber
who that day begged as an embryo-dwarf, [o you who is] the goal obtained
by those who put [their] trust in you
gloss: participial noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect
participial noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect
participial noun, perfective aspect, honorific, third person

en: I, who before did not know any goal, who out of foolishness did not know of obtaining [it], I bowed
saying ‘change’ before the bull among good cowherds
who, going after the woman out of desire, when he twisted [its] neck
by the horns, broke the bull’s neck
When speaking about the meaning that is seen, [there is] the story
of the release of the curse to which the flame-shaped bull rider had fallen
[and] of the bright blood in the curved palm, when our Father, who had vanquished [and] killed seven bulls
filled the opening of the skull mounted [and] eaten by vultures
The great meaning of the stories, Kaṇṇaṉ, is but your name
if one praises in one’s heart what has happened. O Tirumāl
who stands as the sacred word of all stories, humbly
show yourself by great words
gloss: participial noun, neuter plural, perfective aspect

en: I humbled myself before the sacred body. With [my] hand
I lovingly put a fresh lotus on your red feet. I decided on
this: living while praising you desirously, on the lookout for the place to enter
[and] being there, praising
See this, good heart, this birth’s happening
See this, all that we’ve undergone. See this, as a reason
not to come close to hell, reciting the names of Nāraṇaṉ
If you have the strength, look
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, neuter singular
participial noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect
conditional, pronominalised noun, singular, second person

en: I saw the holy body in a dream. There, in his hand
I saw the flaming, glowing discus. I saw
the strength of him who drives away pain [already] experienced [and] the two [kinds of] karma
[and] who moreover blocks further pain
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, imperfective aspect

en: So that the powerful Asuras with swords [and] bright teeth died
he put the powerful bright snake around the powerful bright mountain
to twirl [it] as a churning rod [and] churned the sea
the king who broke the tusk of the murderous elephant
Even as kings, who, having become kings [and] protecting the vast land
move on horse back in front of our eyes, his people
through all seven births cover with cool lotuses only the red feet
of him in whose navel dwells a red lotus flower
In the heart of his people are Tañcai as the first, [Tiruv]araṅkam, Taṇkāl
in the heart of his people are the cool [Vēṅkaṭam] mountain, the [milk] sea
in the heart of his people are Māmallai, Kōval and ramparted Kuṭantai: they say
[these are] the places of our Father who has the power of command
While in the left hand the right-spiralling conch roars constantly, the flame-spitting
discus subdues those who don’t give in at the time when the Appearance
on the bed [that is] a serpent with poison-spitting fire mouths extends
[his] long flower foot in order to measure the directions
gloss: participial noun, negative, honorific, third person
participial noun, causative, neuter singular, perfective aspect

en: When, knowing the time, the monkeys enter flower pools, cut off the buds
blooming there [and] praise with them, [then it is] time, heart
to go to the blossom feet of him from the sapphire[-blue] Vēṅkaṭam
selecting the names of him from ornate Vēṅkaṭam
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: Selecting [them] I speak the thousand names, beginning, middle [and] end
daily strewing available blossoms I who decided
to be a servant to the lord, the great man who set free
the red-eyed elephant, with crescent moon tusks, he had encountered
I did penance through all seven births, all the time
I possess penance; I spoke, for the two feet
of our great lord, a good garland in great Tamil
I who am very good, a [speaker] of great Tamil
See Tiruvēṅkaṭam
where the bull elephant with rising musth stands in front of [his] dark cow
bends the young bamboo with big knots [and] offers [it to her]
mixed with the honey that was nearby
the mountain of the one with a mixed cloud colour
Gathering [and] bringing mountain sandal paste, heavenly vessels/jewels, silk
and white jasmine that abounds in fragrance
reciting [and] making obeissance to the two feet
of the knowing one who stood there in the beginning is desirable
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, singular, masculine
neuter singular, imperfective aspect, verbal noun

en: The good foot of the Highest one is desirable see, good heart
[Worshipping] is desirable see with bright lotus. It is desirable see
to praise humbly, to always proclaim his names, to speak the
twice five hundred as [an act of] penance
Doing penance, the one with four faces obtained the golden feet
that rose [and] extended to measure the earth. With all of his
reddened hands, he completely washed [them] after having poured
Ganges water [and] after having spoken all [his] names
gloss: singular, masculine, third person, perfective aspect

en: [His] appearance without equal for the beauty of [his] shoulders
[he] who stood by his word to her with [bee-]swarmed blossoms with big bamboo shoulders who begged [him]
standing in front of him, the one who did not listen when [his] mother stood behind him [and] begged him
is equal to the huge earth itself that was measured by him
gloss: participial noun, feminine singular, imperfective aspect

en: I consented to servitude, I thought ‘that is bright lotus’
I belonged at your red feet, lovingly. For those who have seen
the full beauty of [your] feet, what of the earlier day
when they had [only] seen the beauty of [your] body?
gloss: participial noun, dative, third person, perfective aspect

en: I saw the day. I saw Nāraṇaṉ. In [my] dream
I often saw him again for real/in the flesh. I often saw
the light form that glitters in heaven of him with red feet
shining with light, with the discus that glitters on [his] body
The Lady in the big blossom with shapely beautiful bright large eyes, seeing
the beauty of [his] graceful body, she did not leave for many days. Even after
why would Earth make preparations [and] desire [his] beauty?
There is no lack of beauty
gloss: neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun

en: As [I felt] a lack, I spoke harsh words. Speaking
about Māl, who is said, by the Veda, [to be] thus, I sat
however many days, thinking ‘will he give, even if it is little
the boon that goes [back] to the Dark one?’
The two feet of the brilliant one who, as a lion
mixed with a man, tore open the fool, who, thinking of [his own] strength
[and] energy, did not bow to him, thinking of the boon
are the ambrosia of the great world there
Saying ‘ambrosia’, ‘honey’ and ‘the one with the discus’
saying ‘the one who delighted taking the ambrosia that day’, praising
with a garland of words like ambrosia I worshipped, uttering [it]
in praise of good Māl who is [thus] spoken of
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect

en: The poets who utter [and] compose [poetry], taking day [fresh] blossoms
what is the benefit they obtain by thus excercising? By which penance
shall I see today him of cloud sapphire colour difficult to see
[even] by true penance for those who are learned?
gloss: instrumental, neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun
participial noun, perfective aspect, honorific, third person
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, accusative, third person

en: I do know [him] as of today. Lying in the womb
I worshipped, hands [folded], the sacred feet that had measured
the big earth, going there that day. I saw
the form of our Father in Tirukkōṭṭi
It alters, [that] I have now understood the entrance door
to the protected city of celestials, before he goes, repelling hell
unavoidable ruin except for those who go [their] way without altering
to our Father in Southern [Tiruv]araṅkam
gloss: participial noun, dative, plural, third person, perfective aspect

en: Once angry with Kaṃsa who was excessive in [his] anger
hotly attacking the war elephant [and] breaking [its tusk], according to [his]
station accepting water with the hand at a former time from Māvali
did you not, as a dwarf, take the earth?
gloss: negative, perfective aspect, singular, second person

en: Do I not rule the earth? Do I not, as a celestial for all the celestials
belong inside the heavenly world after approaching
Tirumāl, the Tall one with red eyes, [and] worshipping
hands [folded], our great lord?
So as not to join hell which is difficult [to bear] later on, you who are foolish
early on make an effort to bow before the red feet of him
who measured all these worlds surrounded by the rain[-filled] ocean
before him who took the measure of many treatises
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, plural, second person
participial noun, singular, masculine, third person
participial noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: The one whose nature is praised by the celestials after he earlier on had killed
Kaṃsa with [his] foot, the one who took the bird on [his] banner, the Tall one
praise only his names! If you praise, the [object of]
desire you wish for shows itself quickly
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect

en: Harsh is cruel hell. Before you join it at a later time
thinking ‘[this] action is cruel’, praise as is fit the one
who took the shapely conch, who tore [apart] the mouth of the one with a mane
who drank the poison from the breast [of the demoness]
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, accusative, third person
masculine singular, accusative, perfective aspect, noun

en: Bow as is fit [and] worship the one with the colour of clouds
who swallowed all seven worlds whole, my heart
that praises him who was in beautiful Pāṭakam after having seized
[and] dug up the chest, he who did not agree
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, accusative, perfective aspect

en: The inhabitant of my heart, the one in my head, he with sapphire colour
who had once torn [open] the strong heart of the Dhānava, he from a distant
aeon [is the one] who puts the aeons into motion, the one with the discus
whom the world praises, whose village is Atti
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: The one whose village is Atti, who mounts the bird, who sleeps on the snake
with hood spots like decorative gems, who is the Veda
of the three fires, who is the lord of the one who ate the poison
from the big ocean, [he is] our Lord
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, imperfective aspect
participial noun, masculine singular, imperfective aspect
participial noun, imperfective aspect, singular, masculine, third person
participial noun, imperfective aspect, singular, masculine, third person

en: You [are] our great lord, the leader of the Unblinking ones
red-eyed tall Māl, you with Śrī on [your] chest, you joined
the bed [that is] a snake with a thousand mouths [and] noses, with rising hoods
taking Kuṭamūkku as a temple
gloss: participial noun, negative, honorific, third person
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, vocative, third person

en: Taking [butter] to strengthen himself he grew as a child
he took [and] ate all the seven worlds so that they were compressed inside [him]
the lord who, dancing on a pot/with pots(?) as a cowherd
stayed [and] took my heart as [his] place
gloss: neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun
neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun

en: While those who don’t blink stand in order [and] strew [bee-]swarmed blossoms
saying ‘lord, our great lord, grace [us]’, Māl, the one with red feet
with clinking anklets, the red-eyed Tall one, in the form of a dwarf
took the earth from Māvali
gloss: participial noun, negative, honorific, third person

en: ‘O Māl, Tall one, Kaṇṇaṉ, you above the celestials
you with the broad tulsi chaplet, you who brought down
from above the fruits of the wood-apple tree with the calf,’ I said
Without limit indeed is the love I have for you
gloss: pronominalised noun, honorific, dative, third person
